name: Metallic Sunburst
lede: Metallic Sunburst is a golden-brown, named in English for a bright burst of light and carried in our data as a traditional Japanese color, *Hiwacha*, which actually names a finch.

sections.title: A sunburst in English, a finch in Japanese
sections.body:
The English name evokes light itself, a gleam bright enough to call a sunburst [1]. Our library also files this hue as *Hiwacha* (鶸茶), a traditional Japanese name our data translates as "finch-brown," after the brownish plumage of a Cardueline finch [1]. The two names describe the same gold-brown shade from entirely different angles, one from light, one from a bird [1].

Its nearest named neighbors by measured color are [[orange-citrine]] and [[honey-yellow]], both almost the same shade, with [[yellowish-hazel]] and [[fallen-leaf]] close behind [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match in 2,098 of 23,781 paintings, 8.82 percent, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 1,357 [2]. That makes it more common than 93 percent of the named colors we track, one of the most frequently matched colors in the whole archive [2]. It peaks in the 1400s, found in 70 of the 945 paintings we have from that century, 1.3 times the expected rate [2]. Fritz Thomsen is its most devoted painter, carrying it in 6 of his 18 works here [2]. Paintings with Metallic Sunburst are more likely than chance to also carry Shit Brown and Olive-Ocher [2].
